summary: Request: hash-anchored per-tenant audit stream with live redaction sample for SIEM onboarding
description:
Issue summary:
FinVerve Bank is onboarding Redwood audit exports into their internal SIEM. They require a per-tenant, append-only audit stream where each delivered batch is anchored with a SHA-256 chain hash (customer-provided anchor token) that they can independently verify. They also require a live redaction sample demonstrating row-level pseudonymization (PII fields masked reversible under HSM) and a small mapping document showing how Redwood audit fields map to their SIEM schema.

Impact:
FinVerve intends to use the stream for regulatory evidence and will not complete production onboarding until they receive cryptographic anchoring + a live redaction sample. Onboarding delay affects a scheduled go-live for a payments feature in two weeks.

Request / Deliverables:
1) Specification for per-batch hash anchoring format (SHA-256 over canonicalized UTF-8 JSON payload, canonicalization rules included).
2) Example signed manifest for a nightly delta with anchor token reference and manifest signature metadata.
3) Live 1-hour redaction sample (subset of events) with reversible pseudonymization applied and HSM attestation header.
4) Field mapping CSV (Redwood audit fields -> FinVerve SIEM fields) and a sample webhook configuration (headers, cert pinning) for their ingestion.

Attachments provided by customer: sample SIEM mapping, compliance questionnaire, and internal policy notes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer configured tenant export to webhook endpoint in Console (prod, us-east) with default envelope.
2) Customer attempted to pull delta bundle via S3 mirror; received payload but cannot verify integrity because there is no anchor token or canonicalization metadata.
3) Customer requested a reversible pseudonymization sample but received a masked sample without HSM attestation headers.

Observed result: payloads arrive but cannot be independently verified by customer; compliance team block on acceptance.
Expected result: each delivered batch should include an anchor reference + canonicalization metadata and reversible pseudonymization sample should include HSM attestation header so FinVerve can map to their evidence requirements.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: reproduced customer's S3 mirror payload and confirmed manifest lacks canonicalization metadata and anchor hash. Checked export pipeline: manifest generator attaches batch_id, timestamps, and delivery signature but anchor field is only populated for 'signed-ledger' export mode; FinVerve export was configured as 'delta-mirror' (no anchor).
Engineering hypothesis: 'delta-mirror' pipeline omitted anchor by design for performance; adding anchor is low-risk but requires schema bump and a short rollout to Dedicated mirror path.
Tests run: created a dev tenant export in 'signed-ledger' mode and delivered sample manifest to FinVerve. Verified SHA-256 anchor generation and verification reproducible locally. Confirmed reversible pseudonymization pipeline can emit HSM attestation headers when 'hsm-pseudonymize=true'.
Next steps: ENG to propose manifest field names and sample payload; Security to review HSM attestation header format; Support to coordinate delivery window with FinVerve compliance team.
resolution: Pending: engineering to provide proposed manifest JSON schema and a 1-hour reversible-redaction sample by 2026-03-16. Temporary workaround: advise customer to enable 'signed-ledger' export mode which includes anchor hashes; note this mode may increase manifest size and slightly delay write latency.
